messages:
maria.devex: Heads-up — ran into a weird ESM/CJS breakage with the JS SDK and several bundlers when trying to get an edge-runtime sample working. Putting steps and logs below so we can reproduce and triage.

maria.devex: Repro (minimal):
1) node 18, TS project (target es2022)
2) install "@redwood/inference-sdk" (local link to current main)
3) app entry is ESM (type: module) and we build for edge runtime (vite/rollup/webpack5 with target = webworker)
4) import in code: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-sdk'`

Observed: build passes but runtime fails on edge with: 
```
SyntaxError: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/inference-sdk/dist/index.cjs' does not provide an export named 'RedwoodClient'
    at async file:///workspace/edge/handler.mjs:12:20
```

maria.devex: Notes: the SDK publishes both cjs and esm fields in package.json. It looks like bundlers sometimes pick the CJS entry or rewrite imports in a way that the edge (which only supports ESM) fails.

maria.devex: Quick repro link: https://git.internal/redwood-repro/edge-esm-cjs (private). Minimal files included: vite.config.js, tsconfig, simple handler.

jon.sdk: Thanks for the detailed repro — I suspected this. We've had parity issues between our "main" and the ESM build output for a while.

jon.sdk: TL;DR: the published package has `main` -> dist/index.cjs, `module` -> dist/index.esm.js, and `exports` with conditional exports, but rollup/vite sometimes resolve to `main` during SSR/build depending on resolver config. Edge runtimes then load the CJS file as ESM causing the error.

jon.sdk: Short-term suggestions:
- Add an explicit `exports` mapping for the ESM entrypoint at the package root: { "import": "./dist/index.esm.js", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }
- Ensure the ESM build sets `exports` and `module` consistently.

sahil.platform: We should also consider adding a tiny `index.js` wrapper that re-exports the ESM entry when running in ESM contexts so bundlers with quirky resolvers get the right file. But that feels like a workaround.

jen.qa: I reproduced on Vite 4.3.1 and Rollup 3.8 with `build.target = 'es2022'` and `ssr: true` — exact same runtime error. I attached the failing vite build log to the repro repo.

jen.qa: Rollup config that fails for me:
```
export default {
  input: 'src/handler.ts',
  output: { format: 'es' },
  plugins: [typescript(), nodeResolve({ browser: true })]
}
```

jen.qa: Changing nodeResolve to `moduleDirectories: ['dist', 'node_modules']` sometimes flips which file it picks.

maria.devex: Also seeing TypeScript typing weirdness: when importing from ESM entry consumers get incorrect types (they resolve to the cjs .d.ts). So type generation/publishing might be out of sync with the ESM build.

jon.sdk: Agreed. Action plan:
1) Patch release that tightens `exports` map and ensures `types` field points to ESM-compatible d.ts (or dual .d.ts that reference conditional exports).
2) Add a compatibility note in README for bundler quirks and include common fixes for webpack/rollup/vite.
3) Add a small repro test matrix in CI: build with vite/rollup/webpack for `webworker` target and run a smoke ESM load in Node ESM runner.

sahil.platform: For Private deployments / edge targets we should also add a validation step during packaging: attempt to `import()` the package ESM entry in a real esm node process to catch these early.

maria.devex: I can open the patch PR for `exports` + types. Jon, can you draft the CI matrix? I can add the vite/rollup repro to the SDK repo under `examples/edge-bundler-repro` so new changes won't regress.

jon.sdk: Yes — I'll add the CI matrix. Also will add a unit that scans package.json post-build to ensure `exports` isn't missing an `import` key.

jen.qa: FYI deploy-bot flagged a failing canary in staging that looks related (edge lambda started throwing the same error).

deploy-bot: [CI] Canary staging: edge-handler@staging failed 1711071400 — runtime import error. See: https://ci.internal/edge-canary/12345

maria.devex: OK, assigning: maria -> PR for exports/types; jon -> CI checks + docs; jen -> add automated repro test; sahil -> packaging validation script. I'll link PRs in the repro issue.

sahil.platform: One more gotcha: webpack 5 with `experiments: { outputModule: true }` sometimes inverts resolution for packages that don't set `module` field. We should add recommended webpack config snippet to docs.

jon.sdk: Good call. I'll add a section: "Edge & bundler compatibility" with explicit examples for vite/rollup/webpack and a minimal `package.json` example that works.

maria.devex: Great. If anyone has additional logs or stack traces, drop them in the repro issue thread rather than here so we keep this thread concise. :thumbsup:

jen.qa: Will do. Adding the failing vite config + stack trace to the repro repo now.

maria.devex: Thanks everyone — will follow up when PR is open.
